kinds.label: Product
kinds.description: A product: the root of a set of specifications.

kinds.label: Business outcome
kinds.description: A business outcome: a measurable change the product exists to bring about, which its capabilities and journeys serve and its tests or records measure (measured_by). The trace runs from it to a capability or a journey, a use case, the code and the tests.

kinds.label: Journey
kinds.description: A journey: the use cases and handoffs, in order, that take the product's people from a trigger to a result a business outcome measures, across actors and domains. It serves business outcomes as a capability does, and its journey test drives it end to end.

kinds.label: Journey step
kinds.description: One step of a journey, in order on its path, in the journey's words. It carries out one use case or one policy (a handoff), of its own product (carries_out); a step that carries out nothing yet is a use case still to write. Its actors are its use case's, derived; a handoff's actor is the product itself.

kinds.label: Domain
kinds.description: A part of the product with its own model, language and owner, for one business capability: what DDD calls a bounded context. Domains meet only through published events.

kinds.label: Aggregate
kinds.description: The consistency boundary: a cluster of entities changed together as one unit, by one command at a time. Other aggregates follow its changes through events, and refer to it by ID only.

kinds.label: Entity
kinds.description: A record the domain keeps, with an identity: its aggregate's root or one of its children. Its fields are entity_field rows; the value objects it has are the ones its fields are typed with.

kinds.label: Value object
kinds.description: A value with no identity of its own, such as an email address or a money amount, defined by its fields and checked by its constraints when it is created. It has no owner: it exists because entities, events or read models use it as a field's type, and its product follows from its ID.

kinds.label: Constraint
kinds.description: A value object's own rule, checked when the value is created, such as an email address having one @.

kinds.label: Invariant
kinds.description: A rule that holds for one aggregate on every change, enforced by its rule (rule) in the aggregate's code. Uniqueness across records (no two members share an email) is an invariant too, which a unique key of the table may back up.

kinds.label: Specification
kinds.description: A named predicate over one or more aggregates of one domain (Evans), such as Member in good standing. Commands check it before acting, and queries may select by it. It has no owner: it reads its aggregates, and its domain follows from its ID.

kinds.label: Domain event
kinds.description: An unchangeable record that something happened to an aggregate, named in the past tense (Loan opened), raised by its commands. What it carries are event_field rows.

kinds.label: Command
kinds.description: A request to change exactly one aggregate: the one its entity belongs to. It sits under the entity it changes, and checks specifications, raises events and may call domain services, all of its own domain.

kinds.label: Read model
kinds.description: A view of its domain's data shaped for reading, which reads one or more of the domain's aggregates. Its fields are read_model_field rows, and it is stored in a table of its own.

kinds.label: Query
kinds.description: A question asked of one read model, its parent. It changes nothing, and may select by specifications and call domain services of its own domain.

kinds.label: Policy
kinds.description: Whenever an event, then a command (event storming). It belongs to the command it invokes and hears one event: its own domain's, or another domain's published one.

kinds.label: Domain service
kinds.description: Domain logic that belongs to no single entity and is not a yes-or-no check, such as calculating a late fee. Commands and queries of its domain call it; it uses no storage and no outside system.

kinds.label: Storage requirement
kinds.description: What the business needs kept of one aggregate or read model, its parent, and how well: whichever apply of durability (it survives a restart or a crash), atomicity (saved whole or not at all, such as a loan with its outbox event), retention and deletion (how long it is kept, and deleted on request), recovery (backups, and how much may be lost) and capacity (how much, how fast). It is built by its aggregate's repository, or its read model's reader, naming a file that exists and the data store it is stored in, and proved by its storage requirement tests.

kinds.label: Term
kinds.description: A word of the domain's glossary and what it means there, so specs, code and conversation use one language.

kinds.label: Capability
kinds.description: An ordered slice of a domain that groups its use cases, such as Catalog or Lending.

kinds.label: Use case
kinds.description: An actor's goal: its actors (use_case_actor rows), its UC requirements and its flow, the same through every interface that offers it. It changes nothing itself; its flow's steps invoke commands and queries.

kinds.label: UC requirement
kinds.description: One rule a use case must follow, whatever the interface: a step of the use case's own flow fulfills it. A rule only one interface can meet is a view or API requirement, or a rule of that interface's pattern, instead.

kinds.label: Pattern
kinds.description: Behavior several use cases share, stated once: a fixed part, the settings each use case that follows it fills in (its configuration, the known ways it varies) and its slots (the open-ended variation, filled with code against a contract). Its settings are pattern_setting rows, its rules pattern_rule records and its slots slot records.

kinds.label: Pattern rule
kinds.description: One rule of a pattern. Every domain that follows the pattern owes it, with no exception: a rule that holds for only some followers belongs to their use cases, not to the pattern.

kinds.label: Slot
kinds.description: An open-ended part of a pattern, which neither its fixed part nor its settings can express: code fills it against its contract. A technical record that fills it, written by hand, is a fill (fills): accidental complexity recorded where it is owed, and debt until the pattern can derive it.

kinds.label: Interface
kinds.description: A way people or programs use the product, such as its web app, its HTTP API or its command line. It offers use cases (offers), is used by some of the product's roles (interface_actor rows) and follows the pattern that says how a step is carried out through it (follows): its version of each flow it offers is derived from that, never written.

kinds.label: Flow
kinds.description: How its use case is carried out, whatever the interface: the steps on its main path and its alternate paths. A use case has one flow, and each interface that offers the use case has its own version of it, derived from the steps' commands and queries by the interface's pattern.

kinds.label: Flow step
kinds.description: One step of a flow, in order on its path, in the words of the people who take it. It fulfills UC requirements of its own use case, invokes at most one command or query and may exchange with integrations; where it happens is its interface's, derived. A step only one interface can do is a variant: it names that interface.

kinds.label: View
kinds.description: A screen or page a person uses. It has no owner: it exists because it presents commands and queries (presents), so a step that invokes one is carried out in it on a web app or desktop interface, and its product follows from its ID.

kinds.label: View requirement
kinds.description: One rule a view must follow, such as what it shows while loading or a field's limits. The UI components whose code does what it says build it (builds).

kinds.label: Endpoint
kinds.description: An HTTP endpoint that exposes exactly one command or query, its parent. A step that invokes it is carried out through it on an API interface: steps reach it through their command or query, never directly.

kinds.label: API requirement
kinds.description: One rule an endpoint must follow, such as an error's response or a limit on its request.

kinds.label: Integration
kinds.description: An outside system the product exchanges with, such as a payment provider or a mail service. It has no owner: it exists because flow steps exchange with it, and its product follows from its ID.

kinds.label: Data store
kinds.description: Where data actually lives: a database, a bucket, a folder of files, browser storage or memory. Every repository, reader and table names the one it is stored in (stored_in). One that is a service someone else runs, which the user must provide, such as a managed database or a bucket, is reached through its integration (provided_by); one the product owns outright, such as a local file or browser storage, has none.

kinds.label: Repository
kinds.description: Loads and saves its aggregate, whole: the way command handlers reach the aggregate's storage, in the one data store it names (stored_in). It persists exactly one aggregate, linked with persists, and sits under its domain, or, for one several domains share, under the domain that holds what they share.

kinds.label: Data model
kinds.description: Its entity in code: the entity's data, behavior and mapping to its table. A command is carried out by its handler and its aggregate root's data model.

kinds.label: Table
kinds.description: Where an entity or a read model, its parent, is stored, in a database or not; or, under a domain, a table of the domain's own infrastructure that implements no design record, such as its outbox. It is kept in the one data store it names (stored_in). Its columns follow from its parent's fields, a value object's fields flattened into columns, so it stores only what fields cannot say: its keys and indexes (table_key rows). An entity's table holds its rows, the source of truth: a table, normalized, or the browser storage, file or memory that keeps them; a read model's is a projection that can be rebuilt, usually a view over its domain's entity tables, or computed in memory on each load.

kinds.label: Value type
kinds.description: Its value object in code, which checks the value object's constraints when a value is created.

kinds.label: Rule
kinds.description: Enforces its invariant: the rule in its aggregate's code, run by the aggregate's commands before saving, which refuses a change that would break it. Lathe's own rules sit in each aggregate's rules.ts and also run over all data on every load. An invariant is built only through its rule.

kinds.label: Predicate
kinds.description: Its specification in code: a yes-or-no test over the records it is given.

kinds.label: Event type
kinds.description: Its domain event's shape in code; a contract with other domains when the event is published.

kinds.label: Projection
kinds.description: Fills its read model's table and keeps it current, from events or as a view's query. It writes only its own read model's table.

kinds.label: Reader
kinds.description: Reads its read model's table for its query handlers: the way query handlers reach a read model's storage, in the one data store it names (stored_in). It reads exactly one read model, its parent, and nothing else; a query handler reads only through its own read model's reader, and the projection alone fills the table it reads.

kinds.label: Command handler
kinds.description: Carries out its command: an application service that owns the transaction, loads the aggregate through its repository, checks specifications and raises events. What clean architecture calls a use case or interactor.

kinds.label: Query handler
kinds.description: Answers its query from its read model's table: an application service that changes nothing.

kinds.label: Event handler
kinds.description: Carries out its policy: hears the policy's event and sends its command.

kinds.label: Service
kinds.description: Its domain service in code. It never uses a repository or an outside system: its inputs are passed in, and it returns a value or a decision.

kinds.label: UI component
kinds.description: A piece of the user interface that renders one or more views and builds the view requirements its code does (builds). It has no owner: it exists because views use it, and its product follows from its ID.

kinds.label: Endpoint handler
kinds.description: Serves its endpoint: reads the request, calls the command or query handler and writes the response.

kinds.label: Adapter
kinds.description: Talks to its integration's outside system, so the rest of the code does not.

kinds.label: Entry point
kinds.description: A start-up file: what runs first and wires the rest together, such as a server's main file or a desktop app's main process. No design record is implemented by it alone, so it sits under the domain it starts.

kinds.label: Tooling
kinds.description: A dev script or config file outside the running product: a build, a generator, a watcher, or a config of the tools it is checked and tested with, such as a type checker's or a test runner's. Its title and file say what it is.

kinds.label: Standard
kinds.description: A library of rules that holds across the product, such as exact money, a latency budget, logging, error handling or naming. Its type says whether its rules are essential (a quality) or accidental (engineering). What follows one of its rules meets it.

kinds.label: Standard rule
kinds.description: One rule of a standard. Technical records that follow it link to it with meets; its standard rule tests prove it.

kinds.label: Test data set
kinds.description: What some tests start from: the environment, the accounts and the starting records, how to prepare and reset them, and the file that builds them. Tests link to it with starts_from.

kinds.label: Constraint test
kinds.description: Proves its constraint: the values its value object accepts and refuses.

kinds.label: Invariant test
kinds.description: Proves its invariant: a change that would break it is refused, and the aggregate stays as it was.

kinds.label: Specification test
kinds.description: Proves its specification: which records satisfy the predicate and which do not.

kinds.label: Policy test
kinds.description: Proves its policy: when its event happens, its command is sent.

kinds.label: Domain service test
kinds.description: Proves its domain service: from the inputs given, the value or decision it returns.

kinds.label: Storage requirement test
kinds.description: Proves its storage requirement at the level that can observe it: a round trip, a restart, a failed save that leaves nothing behind, a deletion, a restore.

kinds.label: Use case test
kinds.description: Proves its UC requirement, at the level the use case is stated: what the actor does and what the product does in answer.

kinds.label: View test
kinds.description: Proves its view requirement in the view.

kinds.label: Endpoint test
kinds.description: Proves its API requirement at the endpoint: the request and the response.

kinds.label: Flow test
kinds.description: The use case's acceptance test: its flow's main path, end to end, through any one interface that offers the use case, at the level that fits that interface (browser for a web app or desktop, system for an API, a CLI or agent tools). How each other interface carries a step out is proved once per rule and domain by its pattern's rule tests, never per use case.

kinds.label: Journey test
kinds.description: The journey's test: its main path, end to end, from its trigger to its result, across the use cases and handoffs it carries out, at the lowest level that can observe the result (service, system or browser). It proves the journey only; each step's use case and policy is proved by its own tests.

kinds.label: Integration test
kinds.description: Proves an exchange with its integration's outside system.

kinds.label: Pattern rule test
kinds.description: Proves its pattern rule in one domain that adopts the pattern: one test per pattern rule and adopting domain.

kinds.label: Standard rule test
kinds.description: Proves its standard rule in the product's code, such as a scan of the code for what the rule forbids or a test of a place that follows it.

kinds.label: Open question
kinds.description: Something undecided, with the role that decides it. It sits under its product or one of its domains, and may be about any record (the about link). A decided question is removed and its answer written into the records it affects.

stages.label: Discovery
stages.description: The business outcomes the product exists to achieve, each a measurable statement with its measure and target, which its capabilities serve, and the journeys that reach them: the use cases and handoffs, in order, from a trigger to a result.

stages.label: Domain model
stages.description: Domains and their aggregates, entities, value objects, rules (constraints, invariants, specifications and policies), events, commands, read models, queries, domain services and glossary terms.

stages.label: Use cases
stages.description: Capabilities, the use cases in them with their actors and UC requirements, and the patterns use cases and domains follow.

stages.label: Interaction design
stages.description: The product's interfaces and the use cases each offers, each use case's flow and its steps, and the views, endpoints and integrations the steps reach, with their requirements.

stages.label: Technical specification
stages.description: The technical record that implements each design record, such as a command's handler or an entity's table, and the standards code meets.

stages.label: Test plan
stages.description: The tests, one kind per thing tested, each proving exactly its parent, and the test data sets they start from.
